  2. Any motion seeking a council decision to declare a given parcel of land remnant, as well as any public exhibition of the same, must be accompanied by:
    1. A map that is sufficient to identify the parcel, any adjacent parcels owned by council or another public body (such as the NSW Government), and any easements or similar rights over the land and adjacent land.  The map scale must be sufficient to make the site features clear, to enable conscientious decision making (such as 1:500 or less).
    2. a report setting out the basis that each criteria in the Policy for Disposal of Council Land have been met in detail, with analysis that addresses, as a minimum, the Relevant Considerations set out in the Appendix.  Councillors Williams and Lane have set out their expectations in the Appendix to this motion.
  3. Any motion for sale of land must be:
    1. Accompanied by an explanation of how council plans to use funds to reduce inequality in council, support and retain local services or similar public purpose,
    2. If the funds are to be spent on infrastructure, the business case and feasibility assessment of that infrastructure, and
    3. Separately accounted for (“ring fenced”) for those purposes; and
  4. Any motion or budget seeking expenditure from the ring fenced account referred to in item 2 (including a budget) must demonstrate how it meets the purposes set out in the motion (item 2a).

questions from cr lane
            
Question/s or service/s requested:
 
A resident has recently raised the lack of availability of parking for residents on The Point Road, Woolwich, due to (among other things) tradespeople and boat trailers.  Can you please advise:
 
  1. Is council monitoring long-term boat trailer parking?  Has it notified owners of its intent to use its powers under the Impounding Act to remove the boat trailers if they remain beyond 28 days?  If so, can it extend its enforcement works to The Point Road?
  2. Has council considered the expansion of its resident permit schemes?  If not, could council consider expanding the W1 area to The Point Road?
 
RESPONSE:
 
  1. Council Rangers are aware of the issues raised and actively patrol and monitor The Point Road as part of both routine and reactive patrols. Rangers undertake multiple patrols daily, including weekends, and infringement notices have been issued where vehicles or trailers are found to be in breach of existing parking restrictions.
 
In relation to removal and impounding powers. Council rangers will continue to monitor the area.
 
  1. Council staff monitor and review parking occupancy and feedback regarding Resident Parking Schemes. Site observations indicate that most dwelling houses along The Point Road have two or more off-street parking spaces available (such as driveways or garages). 
Under Hunter’s Hill Council's current policy for residential parking permits (including the Woolwich Area W1 scheme), properties with sufficient off-street parking are not eligible for resident permits. Extending the W1 area to include The Point Road would therefore provide little to no benefit for the residents, as few—if any—residents would qualify for permits under the existing eligibility criteria.

Annette Gallard addressed the meeting. An extension of time was moved by Cr Williams, seconded by Cr Lane and carried by majority (Deputy Mayor Priestion and Cr Virgara abstaining from the vote).
 
RESOLVED on the AMENDED MOTION  of Councillor Tatyana Virgara, seconded Councillor Carla Kassab

1. That Council note the Draft Budget 2026-27:
  1. Forecasts a deficit of $1.42 million before capital items
  2. Provides for $5.33 million capital expenditure on a range of renewal, upgrade and new projects
2. Subject to 4 and 5, that Council endorses the following draft plans to be placed on public exhibition for 28 days:
  1. Draft Annual Operational Plan and Budget 2026-27 (including Fees and Charges 2026-27);
  2. Draft Long Term Financial Plan 2026 - 36
  3. Draft Workforce Management Strategy 2025 - 29
  4. Draft Strategic Asset Management Plan 2025 - 35
3. That Council receive a report on the public exhibition outcomes and the final draft plans for adoption at the June 2026 Council meeting. 

4. Prior to exhibition, amend the Operational Plan to:

  1. provide an explanation of the costs associated with development of the Asset Management Plan ($810,000, of which $228,000 is consultant fees) given former AMP less than 5 years old, and

  2. provide an explanation for the $686,900 materials and services, under Software and Information Systems.


5. Prior to exhibition, amend the Long Term Financial Plan to:

  1. capture the developer contribution assumptions in section 2 “Financial Assumptions”, 

  2. add a sensitivity analysis to s5 “Risks and LTFP Sensitivity” to test the impact of a 3% developer contribution (s7.12 contribution) from 2026/7 onwards;

  3. provide an explanation or assumptions for the $29,975,000 in Developer Contributions in 2027/8;

  4. provide an explanation or assumptions for the $11,148,000 of assets for disposal in 2028/9.  As a minimum the list of assets should be provided for the community to be able to adequately comment on this; and

  5. include an amount for reconstruction of the Woolwich Baths pontoon in 2027/8 projections, given this has been indicated to the community and not identified for 2026/7.

 
RECORD OF VOTING

ForAgainst
Mayor Zac Miles
Deputy Mayor Julia Prieston
Councillor Carla Kassab
Councillor Marc Lane
Councillor Carol Tannous-Sleiman
Councillor Tatyana Virgara


Councillor Ross Williams

The Motion was CARRIED

Merilyn Malloch addressed the meeting. An extension of time was moved by Cr Tannous-Sleiman, seconded by Cr Williams and carried by majority (Cr Virgara abstained from the vote).
Jim Sanderson addressed the meeting. An extension of time was moved by Cr Williams, seconded by Cr Lane and carried by majority (Cr Virgara and Cr Kassab abstained from the vote).  

RESOLVED on the MOTION of Councillor Tatyana Virgara, seconded Councillor Carol Tannous-Sleiman

Having regard to the Policy, recent independent valuation advice, strategic property considerations, social infrastructure needs, and the unique governance context, this report recommends that Council:

  1. Resolve to progress disposal of the land in accordance with the Policy for Disposal of Council Land and in accordance with Clause 3.3.1, give public notice (28 days) of a proposal to pass a resolution that would state that the land is surplus to the current or future needs of the Council and the local community and has potential for disposal.
  2. Delegate to the General Manager authority to undertake a preliminary, without‑prejudice negotiation with the City of Ryde to test the potential for a negotiated sale of the land at 4 Pittwater Road, Gladesville, on the basis that any settlement must be at or above the independent valuation advice; and
  3. Report back to Council, advising of the outcome of the public notice process, the without-prejudice negotiation process and if appropriate formally determine the land is surplus to Council's needs.


RECORD OF VOTING

ForAgainst

Deputy Mayor Julia Prieston

","reportContent":null,"minutesDiscussion":"R-20-2026  RESOLVED on the MOTION of Councillor Carol Tannous-Sleiman, seconded Councillor Tatyana Virgara

That Council adopt the Quarterly Budget Review Statement March 2026 including the recommended changes detailed in the body of the report in accordance with clause 203 of the Local Government (General) Regulation 2021. The changes are:
  1. Increasing Council’s net operating deficit excluding capital grants and contributions to $4.28 million predominately as a results of delay in selling remnant land to the next financial year;
  2. Decreasing the Capital Works Program from $12.87 million to $8.99 million, primarily to carryover significant capital works projects for LATM's and other infrastructure to the next financial year; and
  3. Increasing projected capital contributions by $0.95 million as a result of completing capital projects during the financial year.

RECORD OF VOTING

ForAgainst
Deputy Mayor Julia Prieston
Councillor Carla Kassab

None

The Motion was CARRIED

  3. That the making of the rates and charges for the rating year 1 July 2026 to 30 June 2027 be made by Council for Ordinary Rates, Domestic Waste Charges and Stormwater Charges as identified on page 33 to 37 of the Annual Operating Plan and Budget.

  1. That Council places the Draft Clarke’s Point Reserve and Morts Reserve Plan of Management as attached to this report on public exhibition for a period of 42 days commencing from 30 June 2026 to coincide with the Sydney Harbour Federation Trust's exhibition of the draft Woolwich Dock and Parklands Management Plan.
  2. That Council receives a further report at the August 2026 Council meeting outlining submissions received during the exhibition period, any recommended amendments and adoption of the Plan of Management.

An AMENDMENT to the MOTION was moved by Councillor Ross Williams, seconded Councillor Marc Lane:


  1. That Council places the Draft Clarke’s Point Reserve and Morts Reserve Plan of Management as attached to this report on public exhibition for a period of 42 days commencing from 30 June 2026 to coincide with the Sydney Harbour Federation Trust's exhibition of the draft Woolwich Dock and Parklands Management Plan.
  2. That Council receives a further report at the August 2026 Council meeting outlining submissions received during the exhibition period, any recommended amendments and adoption of the Plan of Management.
  3. That Council write to the Sydney Harbour Federation Trust to engage in discussions to license the area adjacent to Cuccinetta.
  4. That Council include in the prohibited uses of the location the use of firearms for any purpose.

RECORD OF VOTING

ForAgainst
Deputy Mayor Julia Prieston
Councillor Carla Kassab
Councillor Marc Lane
Councillor Carol Tannous-Sleiman
Councillor Ross Williams
Councillor Tatyana Virgara

Mayor Zac Miles


The AMENDMENT was CARRIED and became the MOTION

R-35-2026  RESOLVED on the MOTION of Councillor Ross Williams, seconded Councillor Marc Lane

  1. That Council places the Draft Clarke’s Point Reserve and Morts Reserve Plan of Management as attached to this report on public exhibition for a period of 42 days commencing from 30 June 2026 to coincide with the Sydney Harbour Federation Trust's exhibition of the draft Woolwich Dock and Parklands Management Plan.
  2. That Council receives a further report at the August 2026 Council meeting outlining submissions received during the exhibition period, any recommended amendments and adoption of the Plan of Management.
  3. That Council write to the Sydney Harbour Federation Trust to engage in discussions to license the area adjacent to Cuccinetta.
  4. That Council include in the prohibited uses of the location the use of firearms for any purpose.


RECORD OF VOTING

A motion was moved by Mayor Zac Miles, seconded by Deputy Mayor Prieston:

That Council:
 
  1. Receive and note the Submissions Outcome Report included as Attachment 1 to this report.
  2. Note feedback received from the community as part of the public exhibition of the Gladesville Masterplan Planning Proposal and Development Control Plan, and thank all in the community who participated in the consultation process.    
  3. Forward the Planning Proposal included as Attachment 2 of this report to the NSW Department of Planning, Housing and Infrastructure, and request that the NSW Minister for Planning and Public Spaces (as the applicable local plan making authority) make a local environmental plan to give effect to the Planning Proposal.
  4. Adopt Chapter 4.4 of the Hunters Hill Consolidated Development Control Plan, included as Attachment 3 of this report, and make necessary arrangements to implement this Plan. 
  5. Delegate authority to the General Manager to make amendments to the Planning Proposal included as Attachment 2 of this report and Development Control Plan included as Attachment 3 of this report that:
    1. Are minor and do not alter the intent; or
    2. Are required by the Department of Planning, Housing and Infrastructure in order to facilitate making of the Local Environmental Plan referenced within Item (C).
  1. Notes the potential opportunity to further investigate whether a site-specific local provision could be prepared to encourage the coordinated redevelopment of the Massey Street transition area with the Gladesville Village Site, subject to appropriate public benefit, urban design, access, open space and infrastructure outcomes.
  2. Authorises the General Manager, or delegate, to consult with the Department of Planning, Housing and Infrastructure and Council’s legal advisers on the feasibility, form and procedural requirements of any such provision.
  3. Notes that this further investigation does not amend, replace or delay the Planning Proposal for the Gladesville Village Site presently before Council.

Cr Williams foreshadowed a motion:

That Council:
  1. Receive and note the Submissions Outcome Report included as Attachment 1 to this report.
  2. Note feedback received from the community as part of the public exhibition of the Gladesville Masterplan Planning Proposal and Development Control Plan and thank all in the community who participated in the consultation process.
  3. Accepts the community concerns regarding unacceptable outcomes of the proposal and pursues further previously developed outcomes: a lower height scheme option as per Option 2 (page 15) in the Report.
  4. Not proceed with the current high-rise site-specific planning proposal with the NSW Department for Planning, Housing and Infrastructure until an alternative has been identified that addresses the community’s concerns; and
  5. In any future proposal, a DCP for the site must be considered at the same time.
  1. Notes the potential opportunity to further investigate whether a site-specific local provision could be prepared to encourage the coordinated redevelopment of the Massey Street transition area with the Gladesville Village Site, subject to appropriate public benefit, urban design, access, open space and infrastructure outcomes.

Cr Carol Tannous-Sleiman joined the meeting at 07:35 pm.

Cr Julia Prieston left the meeting at 07:41 pm. 
Cr Julia Prieston returned to the meeting at 07:42 pm.

Cr Tatyana Virgara left the meeting at 07:43 pm.

To add an additional point to the motion on the floor that:

9. Prior to submitting the planning proposal:
  1. Amend clause 6.11(3) to replace “70m” with “45m”;
  2. Amend clause 6.11(5) in Attachment 2 (page 27) to add the following words:
    1. Built form over 28m limited to a floorspace maximum of 750m of gross floor area; and
    2. No part of the ground floor of a building that is facing a street or public space is to be used for the purposes of residential accommodation, with the exception of Flagstaff Street; and
  3. Undertake a solar access study of Gladesville Public school between 7am and 9am
  4.  midwinter, and a wind study, and then define the specific parts of the site where built form is permitted to exceed 28m (ie towers), and include this as a map to supplement Figure 12.

An AMENDMENT to the MOTION was moved by Councillor Marc Lane, seconded Councillor Ross Williams:


To add an additional point to the motion on the floor that:

9. Prior to adopting Chapter 4.4 of the DCP, amend as follows:

(a)  add a new clause to section 6.1.12 Transport and Access as follows:

“o. Notwithstanding DCP clause 5.3 (Car parking and vehicle access), the maximum parking rates for land to which this document applies are:
  • 0.8 spaces per 1 bedroom
  • 1 space per 2 bedroom
  • 1.2 spaces per 3 or more bedrooms, and
  • 1 visitor space per 7 units”

(c) Amend 6.1.13 Loading and Basement Access to replace “and/or” with “or” and add to the end “as one consolidated vehicle entry no more than 8m wide”.

An AMENDMENT to the MOTION was moved by Councillor Marc Lane, seconded Councillor Ross Williams:

To add an additional two points to the motion on the floor that:

9.    Council is to undertake the following studies and report back to council within 6 months:
    1. As part of the general DCP review already underway:
      1. adopting lower parking rates in the Gladesville Town Centre and LMR areas to minimise additional traffic congestion, having regard for the studies and recommendations undertaken for this planning proposal;
      2. extending design excellence requirements for the key site to all buildings of a certain size or type (eg: apartment blocks in the LMR reform areas, or buildings over 3 storeys).
    2. The potential for a residential parking scheme within 100m of the key site to reduce spillover effects of parking as recommended in the studies undertaken for this planning proposal,
    3. Public domain improvements as recommended by SCT (p12) particularly:
      1. Converting Massey Lane to a shared zone; and
      2. Safe crossing facilities to Cowell Street.
  1. Council is to investigate, and if determined appropriate, amend (under the delegation granted in item 5 of the motion) the Development Control Plan to:
 
  1. in 3.1.2 South Gladesville Precinct “green gateway” recognise the existing neighbourhood centre on Victoria Road between Manning Street and Sunnyside Street, which is over 500m from the main centre and has its own role in supporting residential growth and supporting walkability.
  2. in Figure 5 in 4.1 provide active frontage corners on Hillcrest Street and Junction Street, in recognition of both the existing active frontages and complementary uses on the Ryde LGA side of the street.
  3. in 4.2 (d) increase the floor-to-ceiling height of a small shop to 3.3m consistent with section 4C of the Apartment Design Guide, or 3.6m consistent with 4.2(c).
  4. in 4.2.2 recognise in interfaces the current residential heights permitted by the LMR reforms,  with words to the effect of “(a) a deep soil setback of 3m and (b) a setback of 12m above the permitted building height of that residential zone in accordance with the LEP or Chapter 6 of the Housing SEPP (whichever is higher)” and amend clause 6.1.5 Secondary Setbacks to be consistent with this (noting it is currently inconsistent with the current 4.2.2).
  5. consider whether section 4 particularly 4.2.3 meets the deep soil recommendations and tree canopy requirements of DPHI, particularly the minimum 3m connected to 6m deep contiguous deep soil and 15% deep soil area (plus a requirement to plant 1 medium tree per 300sqm of site area) in the Urban Tree Canopy Targets and Development Controls Report by Gallagher Studio and Studio Zanardo, 2021
  6. exclude solid facades in 4.3(j) from shopfronts and insert a new clause to address shopfronts, to avoid inconsistency with 4.1.  In doing so consider whether 4.3(m) word “shopfronts” should read “facades”
  7. amend 5.2(c) to distinguish between through-building links and through site links open to the sky.  Through-site links open to the sky are typically 6m wide, the narrowest Scotch Row (Barangaroo) is 5m wide.  Through-building links typically have a height requirement of 2 storeys or 1.5x the width, or 6m. Cross referencing with 6.1.8 would also assist this clause.
  8. amend 5.4 to require paving treatments to include vehicle crossovers consistent with the Design of Roads and Streets Manual
  9. amend 6.1.7 Open Space Network to require a minimum width to the key open space areas, to avoid unintended outcomes like a 6m wide “open space” shared zone being delivered on Massey Street.
  10. amend 6.1.6 to provide guidance on the depth of active use, and the proportion of retail and non-retail use at surface level under 6.1.9 - noting for example that The Canopy development specified a minimum 925sqm of surface level retail for this purpose.
  11. amend 6.1.15 overshadowing of Gladesville Public School to consider activities from 7am as per Ryde Council’s submission

 

R-47-2026  RESOLVED on the MOTION of Councillor Tatyana Virgara, seconded Councillor Carla Kassab

That the amendment to the motion be put to the meeting.

During closed session, one resolution was passed as follows:

R-69-2026  RESOLVED on the MOTION of Councillor Tatyana Virgara, seconded Councillor Carla Kassab

  1. That Council receive and note the outcomes of the Expression of Interest assessment for the Henley Community Centre and Eastern Green.
  2. That Council endorse officers inviting the four preferred proponents, being the respondents considered to most closely meet Council’s strategic shortlisting criteria, to provide further information and participate in face-to-face due diligence meetings.
  3. That the further assessment address each respondent’s capacity to act as a capital and delivery partner, including financial capacity and funding arrangements, commercial and operational feasibility, community access and engagement, delivery timeframes, the development proposal (concept plans) and approval pathway, proposed capital works, maintenance and asset responsibilities, lease expectations, exclusions, dependencies and key risks.
  4. That Council confirm its preference for a flexible, multi-use facility capable of accommodating a broad cross-section of the community, with leisure and recreation areas designed and managed to support different activities and changing community needs over time rather than being permanently dedicated to a single sport or use.
  5. That the further engagement be expressly conducted without commitment by Council to select a preferred proponent, enter into a lease, approve a development outcome or fund any works.
  6. That officers continue discussions, where appropriate, with other respondents regarding potential roles as complementary users, hirers or delivery partners at the Henley facility, or opportunities at other suitable sites within the Municipality.
  7. That a further report be presented to Council following completion of due diligence, setting out the findings, options, financial and property implications, proposed procurement or negotiation pathway, and any recommended next steps.
RECORD OF VOTING
ForAgainst
Mayor Zac Miles
Councillor Carla Kassab

  1. Endorse the Hunter's Hill Council Design Excellence Policy, included as Attachment 1 to this report.

It is recommended that Council;
  1. Notes Council’s appointment as Crown Land Manager for Buffalo Creek Reserve, reserve 56260, confirmed by gazette notice dated 7 August 2026.
  2. Notes that this report satisfies resolution 4 of the 27 July 2026 Council resolution by reporting back following confirmation of Council’s appointment and before commencement of the Plan of Management process.
  3.  Authorises commencement of the Plan of Management process for reserve 56260, including tenure verification, land categorisation, preparation of a draft Plan of Management, Crown Lands consultation, community engagement, public exhibition, review of submissions and a further report to Council.

Mr Tony Hatzis addressed the meeting to respond to the objections and answer questions from the Panel.

The Panel resolved to approve the application with a number of modifications to the recommended conditions in the report, as follows:

  1. Extended Internal Trading Hours Trial

The extended internal trading hours approved by this consent are authorised as a 12-month trial only and apply only to the internal use of the premises during the approved extended hours. This trial approval does not authorise any increase in patron capacity, expansion of the licensed area, extended outdoor trading after midnight, or additional entertainment activity unless otherwise authorised by development consent or another lawful planning approval. This approval is additional to the conditions set out under approval DA20031051.

  1. Patron Transport Management Plan: Before commencement of the extended internal trading hours, a Patron Transport Management Plan must be submitted to and approved by Council. The plan must identify suitable taxi and rideshare pick-up/drop-off management procedures, measures to discourage patrons from waiting in residential streets, and procedures for security or staff to assist orderly dispersal. Any use of the existing loading dock for this purpose must first be supported by Council’s traffic/engineering officer as safe, lawful and operationally suitable.

 

  1. Trial hours: During the 12-month trial period, the premises may operate internally under extended hours from 12:00 midnight and 2.00am the following day on Thursday, Friday and Saturday nights only. For clarity, this condition approves only the additional internal trading period beyond the otherwise approved base hours and does not vary any other approved operating restriction except to the extent expressly stated in this condition. 

 

  1. Commencement and expiry: The trial period commences on the first day the extended internal trading hours are exercised and expires 12 months from that date. Written notification of the commencement date must be provided to Council within seven (7) days of the first use of the extended internal trading hours.

 

  1. Reversion to approved hours: Upon expiry of the trial period, the premises must revert to the approved trading hours applying immediately before commencement of the trial, unless the extended internal trading hours are authorised by a further development consent or another lawful planning approval.

 

  1. No continuation without further approval: The extended internal trading hours must not continue beyond the expiry of the trial period unless authorised by a further development consent or another lawful planning approval. Any application to continue the extended internal trading hours must be supported by evidence demonstrating compliance with the consent conditions and the absence of unacceptable amenity impacts during the trial period.

 

  1. Outdoor areas: All outdoor areas, including the beer garden, terrace, rooftop/deck areas and any operable external areas, must cease use by patrons by 12 midnight. No alcohol is to be served or consumed in outdoor areas after 12 midnight, and outdoor furniture or outdoor areas must not be used by patrons after that time except for emergency egress.

 

  1. Plan of Management: During the approved trial extended internal trading hours, the premises must operate in accordance with the Plan of Management dated 26 April 2026, as amended from time to time as required by Council. 

 

The Plan of Management should be amended to include:

  • A dedicated contact number that the community can call to report complaints or make requests such as noise reduction. A senior staff member is to be available on this contact number at all times during the opening hours of the premises. A sign is to be displayed on both street frontages providing the details of this contact number.
  • All calls received must be placed on the Complaints register identified in Condition 11.
  • Noise monitoring devices must be placed on the site and surrounding properties to the satisfaction of Council.

 

  1. Acoustic controls: During the approved trial extended internal trading hours, the premises must comply with the recommendations of the Acoustic Logic report, Rev 2, dated 2 June 2025, except to the extent varied by any later Council-endorsed acoustic advice. In particular, operable windows and roofs for indoor dining areas must remain closed after 10.00pm; background music within indoor dining areas must not exceed 65 dB(A); DJ music must not exceed a spatially averaged sound pressure level of 80 dB(A); operable glazing and doors must remain closed except for patron ingress and egress while DJ music is operating; DJ music after midnight is permitted internally on the ground level only; all entry doors must remain closed except for patron ingress and egress; and all garbage must be retained within the premises after 10.00pm and removed after 7.00am the following day.

 

Noise monitoring devices must be placed on the site and surrounding properties to the satisfaction of Council.

 

  1. Security and patron dispersal: During the approved trial extended internal trading hours, a minimum of two licensed security personnel must be provided in accordance with the Plan of Management. Staff and security must actively monitor patron behaviour within the premises and in the immediate vicinity of the premises, discourage loitering and nuisance behaviour, and implement measures to ensure the orderly and quiet dispersal of patrons. 

At least one security personnel must be undertaking external patron monitoring during the trial extended hours.

 

The Plan of Management should be amended to reflect this condition.

 

  1. Security log: A security log must be maintained for each night on which the extended internal trading hours are exercised, recording security start and finish times, patrol times, incidents, refusals or removals, patron dispersal actions and any interactions with Police or Council officers. The log must be retained on site and made available to Council or Police on request.

 

  1. Incident and complaint register: An incident and complaint register must be maintained on site and made available to Council and Police on request. The register must record the date and time of each incident or complaint, the nature of the incident or complaint, actions taken by staff and any follow-up measures implemented.

 

  1. Complaints contact: A current complaints contact number must be maintained for the duration of the trial period, displayed at the premises, provided to Council and kept current. All complaints must be recorded in the complaints register and responded to within a reasonable timeframe.

 

  1. Litter management: The operator must inspect and clean the immediate frontage and public domain within 50 metres of the premises within 30 minutes after closing on each night on which the extended internal trading hours are exercised. The inspection must include removal of bottles, glass, takeaway waste and other litter reasonably associated with the premises. Each inspection must be recorded in a log retained on site and made available to Council on request.

 

  1. Trial performance report: During the trial period, a performance report addressing complaints, incidents, security logs, patron dispersal, litter management, acoustic complaints or testing, police call-outs, Council complaints and any corrective actions taken during the trial period must be submitted to Council on a quarterly basis.

 

  1. Trial-specific operation of this condition: The operational management, monitoring and reporting requirements of this condition apply only during, and in connection with, the approved trial extended internal trading hours. If the trial period expires and the extended internal trading hours are not continued by further planning approval, those trial-specific requirements cease to apply, except to the extent they are otherwise required by another condition of consent, liquor licence requirement, Plan of Management or other lawful approval.

 

  1. Regulatory action: Nothing in this condition prevents Council from taking enforcement or regulatory action if non-compliance, demonstrated adverse amenity impacts, repeated substantiated complaints or other unacceptable impacts arise during the trial period.

","reportContent":null,"minutesDiscussion":"Mr Jim Sanderson addressed the meeting.
Ms Deidre Burns addressed the meeting. An extension of time was granted (moved by Cr Prieston, seconded by Cr Williams and carried unanimously).
Mr Steven Palos addressed the meeting.
Ms Claire Glase addressed the meeting. An extension of time was granted (moved by Cr Kassab, seconded by Cr Williams and carried unanimously).
A submission by Ms Liz Hinton was read by Mayor Miles. 

R-87-2026  RESOLVED on the MOTION of Deputy Mayor Julia Prieston, seconded Councillor Tatyana Virgara

That Council;
  1. Receive and note the preliminary assessment of the Council-owned land identified in this report against Council’s Policy for Disposal of Council Land.
  2. Endorse the use of a five-project tranche structure for the next stage of the review, comprising Project 1 - Crown Street / Henley Precinct; Project 2 -Earnshaw Street - Gladesville to Tarban Creek Corridor; Project 3 -Encroachments on Road or Drainage Reserves; Project 4 - Road Reserve Parcels (excluding REM38 - View Street Reserve, Woolwich); and Project 5 -Land zoned for Public Recreation.
  3. Note that endorsement of the project-tranche structure is an endorsement of a staged assessment pathway only and does not constitute a decision to dispose of, lease, licence, reclassify, close, sell or otherwise alienate any land.
  4. Endorse the preliminary pathway identified for each project tranche, subject to the completion of all required due diligence, public notification, consultation, legal review, valuation, utility, heritage, environmental, access and probity requirements, excluding REM38 (View Street Reserve, Woolwich), which is addressed separately in Recommendation 9 below.
  5. Note that public notification under Council’s Policy for Disposal of Council Land must not be framed as an approval to dispose of land and must clearly identify that Council has not made a final decision.
  6. Require any submissions received during public notification or consultation to be considered in a further report to Council before any final determination is made.
  7. Note that any information concerning valuation, commercial negotiation, legal advice, litigation risk, privileged advice, owner-specific negotiation positions, probity strategy or commercially sensitive transaction matters should be reported separately in a confidential report where the requirements of section 10A of the Local Government Act 1993 are met.
  8. Note that any final decision to dispose of Council land must be made by resolution of Council and cannot be delegated.
  9. Exclude REM38 (View Street Reserve, Woolwich) from the next stage of review under Project 4 - Road Reserve Parcels. REM38 is to be retained in Council’s ownership, and no further due diligence or investigation should be undertaken in respect of REM38 as part of this process, in recognition of its existing reserve-like use and the community and local amenity value identified in the report and from the community. This exclusion does not preclude Council from considering the future of REM38 separately at a later date, by way of a further report, should circumstances change.
  10. That Council investigate and provide a report to a future Council meeting regarding the rezoning REM38 to RE1 Public Recreation.


RECORD OF VOTING

ForAgainst
Mayor Zac Miles
Deputy Mayor Julia Prieston
Councillor Carla Kassab
Councillor Carol Tannous-Sleiman
Councillor Tatyana Virgara

Councillor Ross Williams


The Motion was CARRIED

","reportContent":null,"minutesDiscussion":"Ms Karyn A Raisin addressed the meeting. An extension of time was granted (moved by Cr Williams, seconded by Cr Prieston and carried unanimously). 
Mr Nicholas Yap addressed the meeting. An extension of time was granted (moved by Cr Williams, seconded by Cr Kasab and carried unanimously).

R-85-2026  RESOLVED on the MOTION of Councillor Carol Tannous-Sleiman, seconded Councillor Tatyana Virgara

That Council:
 
  1. Recognises that its use of Acknowledgement of Country has become tokenistic and routine rather than meaningful and reflective.
  2. Prepares and places on public exhibition, in accordance with section 361 of the Local Government Act 1993, a draft amended Code of Meeting Practice that gives effect to ensuring Council’s use of Acknowledgement of Country, Welcome to Country and Smoking Ceremonies is meaningful and proportionate, by providing for each practice, as appropriate, to be reserved for use only at significant community and cultural events, such as the Moocooboola Festival.
  3. Reaffirms its commitment to practical and meaningful recognition of the Wallumedegal people by directing the General Manager to:
    1. report on the implementation of the Reflect Reconciliation Action Plan, identifying for each action its status, expenditure, evidence of delivery, outcomes achieved, consultation undertaken and any outstanding work;
    2. establish a Reconciliation Action Plan (RAP) Working Group comprising the Mayor, 2 Councillors, the General Manager, the Director of Corporate and Community and where practicable, a Traditional Owner or authorised representative with knowledge of the Wallumedegal and the local area and another member of the community.
  4. Direct the General Manager to report to Council with the RAP Working Group’s recommendations for a renewed RAP and cultural protocols framework, including practical initiatives such as local heritage education, Indigenous-led programs, partnerships, cultural interpretations and protection of Aboriginal heritage. 
  1. Ensures that any other formal policy amendments necessary to give effect to these Recommendations are reported separately to Council and progressed in accordance with all applicable statutory consultation and public exhibition requirements.


RECORD OF VOTING

ForAgainst
Mayor Zac Miles
Councillor Carla Kassab
Councillor Carol Tannous-Sleiman
Councillor Ross Williams
Councillor Tatyana Virgara

Deputy Mayor Julia Prieston


The Motion was CARRIED
